notable_language.quote: At the 2019 Annual Meeting, 77% of the votes cast supported our advisory resolution on the compensation of our Named Executives (“say-on-pay” vote).
notable_language.why_notable: Discloses a relatively weak say-on-pay result, which the committee then uses to frame the FY21 program changes.

notable_language.quote: In discussing our compensation program throughout 2020 with investors, several key themes emerged in shareholders’ feedback. The Compensation Committee evaluated these themes and implemented enhancements to our fiscal year 2021 compensation program that both respond directly to shareholder input and further increase pay-for-performance alignment at Microsoft.
notable_language.why_notable: The committee's explicit framing of the FY21 metric and weighting changes as responsive to investor pressure rather than its own initiative.

notable_language.quote: The Compensation Committee believes this will strengthen the CEO’s accountability to achieving results on the objective financial metrics that most closely align with our business strategy.
notable_language.why_notable: Stated rationale for shifting the CEO cash incentive from 50% to 70% formulaic financial — implicitly concedes the prior design left more to subjective assessment.

notable_language.quote: In addition, for all of our executive officers, in fiscal year 2021 we have added a downward adjustment to the relative TSR modifier so that payouts will be reduced for TSR performance below the 40 th percentile of the S&P 500.
notable_language.why_notable: Acknowledges the prior TSR modifier gave only upside exposure; the fix is stated as applying to all executive officers, not just the CEO.

notable_language.quote: Where we have strong historical data, as with the Revenue and Operating Income measures used to determine 50% of the annual cash incentive (70% for the CEO in fiscal year 2021), we set thresholds at an estimated 90% probability of payout, and maximums at an estimated 20% probability of payout. Where we do not have strong historical data that will allow for probability estimates, as is the case with our more recently developed PSA metrics, we set thresholds that we believe are reasonably achievable and maximums that we believe can be reached only with esceptional performance.
notable_language.why_notable: Unusually specific disclosure of goal-setting probabilities, and an admission that PSA metric rigour cannot be probability-tested.

notable_language.quote: Due to the dynamic nature of our business and the specificity in the performance metrics that are chosen under our PSA program, we believe that measuring performance annually over our three-year performance period and modifying awards based on our three-year relative TSR results provides the most accurate assessment of our Company’s long-term trajectory and performance achievements.
notable_language.why_notable: Defence of a structure that sets one-year targets inside a nominally three-year long-term award — a recurring point of investor criticism.

notable_language.quote: While Microsoft is constantly striving to lead across our product categories, there is more work to do in driving solutions that will get Microsoft to market faster.
notable_language.why_notable: A rare explicit criticism embedded in the CEO's operational scorecard rationale, accompanying the lowest of his three category scores (130%).

notable_language.quote: The Board asked Mr. Nadella to create additional focus on the culture of the organization for fiscal year 2020 and is very pleased with the results that were achieved.
notable_language.why_notable: Shows the Board setting a non-financial priority directly and rewarding it with the highest operational score (160%).

notable_language.quote: While this market analysis and supplemental data inform the decisions of the independent Board members and our Compensation Committee on the range of compensation opportunities, we do not tie executive officer compensation to specific market percentiles.
notable_language.why_notable: Hedge that preserves discretion in pay setting while disclosing peer benchmarking.

notable_language.quote: For fiscal year 2021, the Compensation Committee reviewed the evolution of our business against our historical peer group, and as a result approved the use of two peer groups with two components to better reflect the differentiated business, talent and, in some cases, pay models, across sectors:
notable_language.why_notable: Explains a structural change in benchmarking — splitting into technology and general-industry peer groups — as reflecting business evolution.

notable_language.quote: The technology labor market is hyper-competitive with demand growing faster than the supply of technical talent, resulting in significant increases in compensation at the companies with whom we compete for this talent.
notable_language.why_notable: Management's own competitive-market framing, used to justify pay levels; the phrasing is the kind that recurs and shifts across years.

notable_language.quote: However, the changes implemented to Section 162(m) under the TJCA are expected to significantly limit deductibility of compensation paid under current and future awards to covered employees. Accordingly, our Committee awards compensation that is nondeductible.
notable_language.why_notable: Unusually blunt statement that the committee knowingly grants non-deductible pay.

notable_language.quote: Mr. Nadella articulated this purpose as the creation of profitable solutions to the challenges of people and planet in every community in every country around the world.
notable_language.why_notable: Purpose language new to the CD&A framing, tied directly to the Customers & Stakeholders scoring rationale.

notable_language.quote: Success in fiscal year 2020 required – more urgently than almost any other year – intense focus on business operations, agility to adapt to rapidly changing circumstances, strategic vision and excellence, and advancement of a world view that embraces challenges bigger than the Company, some that linger from our past and others that loom in our future.
notable_language.why_notable: The committee's summary justification for FY20 pay outcomes, invoking pandemic-year difficulty rather than metric results alone.
